key_insight: Stacking ensemble learning outperformed the multitask neural network on all three welding-property predictions, with the largest improvement in ultimate tensile strength (UTS).
engineering_relevance: Predicting UTS, weld hardness, and heat-affected zone (HAZ) hardness can support welding process assessment and structural-integrity decisions.
method: Compare multitask neural networks and stacking ensembles on a shared welding dataset.
Use shared hidden representations with task-specific outputs in the multitask network.
Evaluate each property using RMSE and R².
evidence_signal: Stacking achieved R² values of 0.9863, 0.9782, and 0.8453 for UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, respectively, versus 0.6724, 0.9215, and 0.8407 for the multitask network.
watch_item: The abstract omits dataset size, validation protocol, and RMSE scaling, limiting assessment of generalizability and practical error magnitude.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
